0.long_answer: The congenital heart defect most commonly associated with a holosystolic murmur best heard at the left lower sternal border is a ventricular septal defect (VSD). In VSD, there is an opening in the interventricular septum that allows blood to flow from the high-pressure left ventricle to the lower-pressure right ventricle, creating a left-to-right shunt. This abnormal flow produces the characteristic pansystolic (holosystolic) murmur heard along the left lower sternal border, and its intensity can vary depending on the size of the defect. VSDs are among the most common congenital heart anomalies and can range from small defects that may be asymptomatic to larger defects that can lead to heart failure and pulmonary hypertension.
